potential_unspecified_behavior: The core addon subpage route (frontend/src/app/drive/[name]/addons/[addon]/[slug]/page.tsx) renders null while the dynamic import is pending and calls notFound only after the import rejects. With pages/find deleted, the bundler's import context no longer contains find, so the import rejects. This is unchanged code and matches spec item 2.
regression_risks: Coverage floors (addon COV_FLOOR, core vitest thresholds) may drop because tested code was removed. Spec D3 covers this, but I did not check whether the floors were adjusted.
Merge order D2: the addon's CI depends on frontend/src/__tests__/search-modes-entries.test.ts having been deleted from core develop first (commit b9b776446 appears to do this).
test_coverage: I1: Page.test.tsx 'SPEC-ADDON-158 I1' renders the Ask page with a drive and without one. It asserts no tablist, no tab, no Ask/Find link and no href containing /addons/intelligence/find, plus the title and icon. Reinstating the ModeTabs render would fail it.

I2 (addon side): retireFind.searchModes.test.tsx renders AddonSlot search-modes from the manifest and from a stale catalogue naming find-mode. Re-adding find-mode to slots.ts would render a menuitem and fail the test.

I3: the backend test uses a synthetic _test addon, so it proves the generic proxy 404s an undeclared route, not the intelligence manifest specifically. Together with I5's manifest check it covers the claim. The grep test walks the four client roots and excludes test files.
I4: page.retireFind.test.tsx checks that the find slug reaches notFound and that pickup still loads.

I5: the test asserts only the absence half. 'Every other slots entry and proxy.routes entry is unchanged' has no test, so an accidental edit to another route in this diff would not be caught (by reading, the diff touches no other entry).
I6 (in-file find unchanged): no new SPEC-ADDON-158 test exists. It relies on the existing file_find tests.
